/-!
# Erdős Problem 673

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/673](https://www.erdosproblems.com/673)
- [Er79e] Erdős, Paul, _Some unconventional problems in number theory_. Astérisque (1979), 73-82.
- [Er82e] Erdős, Paul, _Some of my favourite problems which recently have been solved_. (1982),
  59--79.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter Asymptotics Real

namespace Erdos673

/-- If $1=d_1<\cdots <d_{\tau(n)}=n$ are the divisors of $n$ (here `Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i` is
$d_{i+1}$), then
$$G(n) = \sum_{1\leq i<\tau(n)}\frac{d_i}{d_{i+1}}.$$ -/
noncomputable def G (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i : Fin (n.divisors.card - 1), (Nat.nth (· ∣ n) i : ℝ) / Nat.nth (· ∣ n) (i + 1)

/--
Let $1=d_1<\cdots <d_{\tau(n)}=n$ be the divisors of $n$ and
$$G(n) = \sum_{1\leq i<\tau(n)}\frac{d_i}{d_{i+1}}.$$
Is it true that $G(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$?

The answer is yes: Tao observed that $\tau(n/m)/m\leq G(n)\leq \tau(n)$ for any $m\mid n$, so
that $G(n)$ behaves very similarly to $\tau(n)$. In [Er82e] Erdős recalls this conjecture and
observes that it is indeed trivial that $G(n)\to \infty$ for almost all $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos673.lean#L914"]
theorem erdos_673.parts.i : answer(True) ↔ ∀ C : ℝ, {n : ℕ | C < G n}.HasDensity 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Can one prove an asymptotic formula for $\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)$?

Indeed $\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)\sim X\log X$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos673.lean#L914"]
theorem erdos_673.parts.ii :
    (fun X : ℕ ↦ ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X, G n) ~[atTop] fun X : ℕ ↦ (X : ℝ) * log X := by
  sorry

/-- Erdős writes it is 'easy' to prove $\frac{1}{X}\sum_{n\leq X}G(n)\to \infty$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
  "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos673.lean#L914"]
theorem erdos_673.variants.average :
    Tendsto (fun X : ℕ ↦ (∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 X, G n) / X) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/-- Tao observed that, for any divisor $m\mid n$, $\frac{\tau(n/m)}{m} \leq G(n) \leq \tau(n)$. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_673.variants.tao (n m : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (hm : m ∣ n) :
    ((n / m).divisors.card : ℝ) / m ≤ G n ∧ G n ≤ n.divisors.card := by
  sorry

end Erdos673

findings.description: The divisor hypothesis `hm : m ∣ n` permits `m = 1`, but the lower bound requires a nontrivial divisor. Taking `n = m = 1` satisfies both hypotheses and gives `1 ≤ G 1`, whereas `G 1 = 0` because its sum is empty. This is not merely an issue at `n = 1`: taking `n = 2, m = 1` gives the false inequality `2 ≤ 1/2`. Both counterexamples were verified in Lean without using any sorry-backed theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős [Er79e], pp. 73–74, defines the statistic as the sum of consecutive-divisor ratios, with τ(n)−1 summands (https://www.numdam.org/item/AST_1979__61__73_0.pdf). The file's cited external solution explicitly states “Tao's lower comparison, with the necessary hypothesis `m > 1`”: its `tao_lower_bound`, lines 257–261, assumes `(hn : n ≠ 0) (hm : 1 < m) (hmn : m ∣ n)` before asserting τ(n/m)/m ≤ G(n). See https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/8822f7ddef30fadbd92e1c6ab4ed897af356af5e/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos673.lean#L257-L261.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a hypothesis `(hm_gt_one : 1 < m)` to `erdos_673.variants.tao`. Keep the existing conclusion and positivity/divisibility hypotheses. Also qualify the descriptions of this bound in this theorem's docstring and the docstring of `erdos_673.parts.i` with `m > 1`.

reformulations.difference: [Er79e], p. 74, asks that the statistic tend to infinity after discarding one sequence of density zero. Lean instead requires that each fixed superlevel set `{n | C < G n}` have density one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: These are equivalent by a diagonal construction, not by simply taking a countable union of exceptional sets. Let B_k = {n | G(n) ≤ k} for positive integers k. Each B_k has density zero, and the B_k are nested. Choose strictly increasing N_k so that for every N ≥ N_k, |B_k ∩ [0,N)|/N ≤ 1/k. Set E = ⋃_k (B_k ∩ [N_k,N_{k+1})). For N in the kth interval, E ∩ [0,N) is contained in B_k ∩ [0,N), so E has density zero. Outside E, G(n) tends to infinity. Conversely, convergence outside a single density-zero set puts all but finitely many points of a density-one set into every fixed superlevel set, giving exactly the Lean condition.

demonstrated.claim: The declaration is false: n = m = 1 satisfies its hypotheses, but its lower bound becomes 1 ≤ G 1 = 0.

submission.summary: /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean proves the negation of the declaration's exact type using type_of%. The file compiles without errors or warnings.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«673»

/-! A counterexample to the divisor bound in Erdős problem 673. -/

-- Erdos673.erdos_673.variants.tao is false: n = m = 1 satisfies its hypotheses,
-- but its lower bound is 1 ≤ G 1 = 0, since G 1 is an empty sum.
example : ¬ (type_of% @Erdos673.erdos_673.variants.tao) := by
  intro h
  have h11 := (h 1 1 (by decide) (by decide)).1
  norm_num [Erdos673.G, Finset.sum_fin_eq_sum_range] at h11

submission.summary: Added the necessary hypothesis `hm_gt_one : 1 < m` to Tao's divisor bound and updated both docstrings describing that bound. The edited file compiles with no errors and only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
